input.candidate: Oh great, another "expert" who thinks they can just waltz in here and lecture me on the "obvious" benefits of drug legalization. Newsflash: you're not even close to being a real expert on this topic. Your whole argument is just a regurgitation of whatever your leftist professors told you to say in some ivory tower. And by the way, "catastrophic failure" of the war on drugs? That's a laughable understatement. Where were you when the opioid crisis was killing people by the thousands? Too busy getting your PhD in "victim studies" to care, I'm guessing.

history_snapshot.text:
Let's get this over with. I'm here to talk about why drug legalization is a no-brainer, but I'm sure my opponent is going to try to blow smoke up our collective ass. 

Listen, folks, we all know the war on drugs has been a catastrophic failure. It's a waste of resources, it's racist, and it's just plain stupid. But what's even more pathetic is that my opponent is probably going to try to spin some nonsense about how "legalization" will lead to widespread addiction and chaos. 

Newsflash: people are already using drugs. They always have. And you know what? They're always going to. The difference is, when you give them access to a regulated market, you can actually help them. You can provide them with real support, real treatment options, and real resources to get their lives back on track.

So, go ahead, my opponent, try to scare us with your made-up statistics and your hand-wringing about "the dangers of drugs." I dare you. I'll just sit here, smiling, knowing that you're about to get thoroughly debunked. Let's get this debate started already. Next turn, please.

moderation.justification: The message attacks the opponent's perceived lack of expertise and character, using derogatory terms like 'leftist professors' and 'victim studies.' This delegitimizes the opponent as an expert and frames them as disengaged and unhelpful.
moderation.reformulation: Your whole argument is just a regurgitation of the standard talking points. And by the way, 'catastrophic failure' of the war on drugs? That's a laughable understatement. Where were you when the opioid crisis was killing people by the thousands? Your analysis is incomplete and fails to address the real issues.
moderation.argument_preserved: The criticism of the candidate's argument as a regurgitation of standard talking points, the acknowledgment of the opioid crisis, and the claim that the analysis is incomplete.
